outcome: Vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) success rate
cohort: The study included 220 women with one previous lower segment caesarean section attempting vaginal birth and a control group of 155 women without a previous caesarean section.
finding: Attempting a vaginal delivery after one previous lower segment caesarean section in women experiencing spontaneous active labour can achieve a considerable success rate without significantly increasing adverse outcomes for mother and foetus.
mod_finding: The VBAC success rate in the study group was 80%, with 20% requiring repeat caesarean section, mainly due to intrapartum fetal distress, and a low incidence of uterine complications (1% dehiscence, 0.5% rupture).
